rules: The Title Descriptor dataset provides estate interest and class of title for registered estates and interests in England and Wales.
Class of title expresses the Registrar's confidence in ownership established at registration.
A unique title number can have only one class of title.
The dataset is a subset of the Land Register covering registered land and property titles.
Every completed registered title has a title number, estate interest and class of title.
A pending registration can have a title number while estate interest and class remain absent.
The dataset also represents registration applications started but not yet completed.
The Title Descriptor product is closely linked to National Polygon and UPRN products.
Title number is the cross-product identifier used to link HMLR datasets.
The documented class diagram contains title number, estate interest, class of title, registered status and change indicator.
Title number is a mandatory character field.
Estate Interest is a non-mandatory character field.
Class of Title is a non-mandatory character field.
Registered status is a mandatory character field.
Registered status value Pending means the application is being processed.
A blank registered-status value means the title is registered.
Change Indicator is a mandatory character field.
Change Indicator values describe New, Changed or Deleted rows.
Estate-interest code EL means an estate in land.
A freehold estate is held for an unknown or infinite duration.
A leasehold estate has a fixed or maximum duration.
Code FA is an affecting franchise tied to a defined area and does not convey ownership of physical land.
Code FC is a relating franchise not tied to a defined area and distinct from ownership of physical land.
Code MA denotes a manor; the Land Registration Act 2002 provides no power to register a manor.
Code PG denotes a profit a prendre in gross, such as a right to fish or take something from another's land.
Code RC denotes a rentcharge payable annually or biannually as a charge on land.
Code RP denotes a perpetual rentcharge intended to continue indefinitely.
Code RT denotes a terminable rentcharge granted for a fixed number of years.
Code AF is absolute freehold, the best class of freehold title.
Absolute freehold commonly relies on proper documentary title with a good root at least 15 years old at acquisition.
Code QF is qualified freehold where a specific defect prevents absolute title.
Code PF is possessory freehold, commonly arising from adverse possession or lost or destroyed deeds.
Code AL is absolute leasehold, the best class of leasehold title.
Absolute leasehold requires an acceptable estate title and approval of the lessor's title to grant the lease.
Code GL is good leasehold where assignment is shown but evidence is insufficient for absolute leasehold.
Code QL is qualified leasehold where the lessor's reversion or lessee's interest has a specific defect.
Code PL is possessory leasehold where possession substitutes for conventional documentary title.
Code SF is a freehold scheme title built up as freehold land is acquired piecemeal.
Code CF is commonhold freehold ownership with collective management of common areas.
Code SL is a leasehold scheme title built up as leasehold land is acquired piecemeal.
Code CL is the documented commonhold leasehold class.
Code AR is absolute rentcharge, the best class of rentcharge.
Code PR is possessory rentcharge where conventional documentary evidence is unavailable.
Code QR is qualified rentcharge where an application for absolute rentcharge has a defect.
Code CN is a caution against first registration so the cautioner receives notice of an application.
HMLR states that public data accuracy is pursued but freedom from errors or fitness for purpose is not guaranteed.
First registration records whether land is held freehold or leasehold.
The specification identifies three freehold classes and four leasehold classes.
Absolute is the best class of title.
Qualified title can be granted where a specific defect is recorded in the register.
Possessory title applies to adverse possession or lost or destroyed title deeds.
Good leasehold can apply where evidence of the landlord's right to grant the lease is unavailable.
The tenure of a title does not change within the dataset's maintenance model.
A non-absolute class can be upgraded after an application supported by appropriate evidence.
Each month HMLR publishes a full extract, change-only update and validation file.
Where data changes more than once in a month, only the latest state is published.
Dataset access requires an account, licence agreement and payment.
Updated files are available from the second working day of each month.
Title Descriptor files are delivered in CSV format.
Full, change-only and validation files use the documented LR_TENURE naming patterns.
The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 planning and housing datasets through one interface.
Latitude and longitude queries return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Multiple dataset parameters return matches from any selected dataset covering the point.
The documentation describes UPRN queries as more precise than coordinate queries for registered properties.
Entity responses include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
An empty result must not be treated as proof that no planning constraints exist because coverage varies.
The documented discovery request fetches all 337 local planning authorities.
geometry_entity reuses an existing entity geometry for spatial filtering.
Listed-building entities expose a listed_building_grade field in the entity response.
The planning-application data specification is still in development and may change.
Local planning authorities are not currently required to share application data to that specification.
Planning application searches can use year, month, day and match mode for start-date filtering.
Custom-area geometry uses WKT and request spaces must be percent-encoded.
Planning geometry-query coordinates are documented in WGS84 EPSG:4326.
Pagination advances offset by the selected limit.
Responses provide next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The API has no portfolio batch endpoint and requires one request per property.
The documentation instructs clients to apply polite rate limiting.
For large portfolios, bulk downloads enable local intersections and a stable snapshot.
Bulk downloads are offered as CSV, JSON and where applicable GeoJSON and Parquet.
The 2m composite DSM covers approximately 99 percent of England.
The 2m composite DSM uses the last or only laser return.
The DSM includes vehicles, buildings and vegetation as well as terrain.
The product combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist, the newest best-resolution data is selected.
Resampled source data is bilinearly interpolated before merging.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 through 2 April 2022.
The product is distributed as GeoTIFF rasters in 5km OS National Grid tiles.
Values are metres above Ordnance Survey Newlyn using the OSTN15 transformation.
Input LIDAR surveys state vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The metadata record states no public access constraints, subject to the identified licence.
The 2m DTM removes surface objects using bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
Metadata index catalogues identify which survey contributed at a location.
The 2m first-return DSM uses the first or only laser return and retains surface objects.
National-programme surveys are merged with feathering across overlaps to reduce elevation differences.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset for Great Britain.
Grid and contour products are created from the same source data.
Tiled supplies use the National Grid reference of the south-west tile corner.
The grid consists of heighted points at regular 50m post spacing.
The contour product uses 10m interval standard contour polylines.
Contours include mean high and low water boundaries and spot heights.
The product is free to use for commercial, educational and personal purposes.
Maintenance is linked to an integrated three-to-five-year flying programme.
The overview states full Great Britain coverage.
OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
OS Terrain 50 grid data has been verified at 4m RMSE.
The source DTM is captured as a triangulated irregular network using mass points and breaklines or automated methods.
The bare-earth model excludes buildings, supported structures and vegetation.
Grid tiles do not overlap and do not share common edge values because heights are calculated at pixel centres.
GML feature identifiers are unique within a release; whole-tile refresh regenerates sequential identifiers and no feature-level COU is planned.
